welcome, traveler

How to Keep This Grimoire

This is a working book — print it, bind it, spill tea on it.
It is meant to grow moss and marginalia.

Print what you need, as often as you need. Every page is undated and reusable. Print a fresh plant profile for each new ally you meet; print twelve moon trackers for a year of moons.

The Materia pages (plant profiles & field identification) are the heart of the book — one spread per plant, gathered over seasons into your own local materia.

The Field pages (trip log, seasonal calendar, ethics) travel with you. A clipboard and a pencil in the woods beat a perfect binder at home.

The Hearth pages (teas, salves, simmer pots) record what you make from what you gather — with dates, ratios and results, so your craft compounds.

The Workings pages (spell log, correspondences, sigils, dreams) keep the subtle side of the practice. Note moon and season; patterns emerge in the margins.

Bind it your way — three-ring binder, discbound, or a simple folder. The contents page at the front is a fill-in index: number your pages as your book grows.

A note on printing — pages are designed for US Letter or A4, single-sided,
in ink-friendly near-black. Cardstock makes fine covers; 24 lb paper takes fountain pen well.

the forager's oath

Ethics of the Wild Harvest

The first rule of the hedge: the land is not a shelf.
Take as a guest, not as an owner.

Be certain, then be certain again. Identify by at least three features and one trusted guide before anything touches a basket — and never trust an app alone with your life.

Take a tithe, not a harvest. One in ten, never the first found, never the last standing. Leave the grandmother plants to seed the next hundred years.

Know whose land you stand on — legally and historically. Ask permission where permission is needed; tread lightly where it is given.

Leave protected species be. Learn your region's at-risk list and let rarity be a boundary, not a trophy.

Harvest clean. Skip roadsides, sprayed verges, dog-walked strips and downstream of runoff. The plant remembers where it grew.

Do no harm getting there. Stay on durable ground, close the gates, fill your holes, pack out more than you brought.

Give something back. Water, a scattered seed, a cleared tangle of litter — the old bargain, kept small and often.

My own rules — added as the land teaches them

From the Eldwyld Archives

The Forager's Grimoire was made in the Eldwyld — a realm kept at the crossroads of imagination and implementation, where the mystical and the digital converge. It was designed to be printed, bound, carried into wet grass, and filled with a life's worth of green knowledge.

Your license

This grimoire is licensed for personal use: print as many copies as you wish, for yourself and for gifts, forever. Please don't resell, redistribute, or upload the files themselves — send fellow travelers to the Archives instead.

A necessary word of care

Nothing in these pages is medical advice, and no journal replaces a qualified guide, an up-to-date regional field manual, or common sense. Foraging carries real risk: misidentification can be fatal. You are the only one responsible for what you harvest and what you do with it.

Print notes

US Letter and A4 editions included · single-sided · near-black ink on any paper · pairs well with a three-ring binder, pressed leaves, and a pot of something warm.
